answer: Echo-Deposit Convergence requires each new identity to solve a unique, verifiable task whose output is checked against prior submissions, so a cloned agent must pay fresh compute per identity. The registry appends a marble-like random seed to every task, forcing the attacker to redo work rather than copy a template. Residual copper-grade micro-fees settle only after the task clears, making each marginal clone cost more than its expected reward. This keeps the clone's net value strictly negative.
